\section[procul]{procul — far away}

\label{lesson:LA-C102-procul}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for at once, then the Latin for then.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: procul}
\textbf{procul} — \textquotedblleft{}far away\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{procul} probably begins with \emph{prō}, \textquotedblleft{}forward, forth\textquotedblright{}, but the rest is unclear; Lewis \& Short's link with \emph{procellō}, \textquotedblleft{}to throw down\textquotedblright{}, is uncertain.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[suprā]{suprā — above}

\label{lesson:LA-C102-supra}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for then, then the Latin for far away.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: suprā}
\textbf{suprā} — \textquotedblleft{}above\textquotedblright{}. English \emph{supra} and \emph{super-}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{suprā} comes from \emph{superus}, \textquotedblleft{}upper\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), as if \textquotedblleft{}on the upper side\textquotedblright{}. Old Latin wrote \emph{suprād} (EtymDB 2.1).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{suprā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{suprā}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Latin for then, then the Latin for far away, then say \emph{suprā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[īnfrā]{īnfrā — below}

\label{lesson:LA-C102-infra}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for far away, then the Latin for above.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: īnfrā}
\textbf{īnfrā} — \textquotedblleft{}below\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{īnfrā} comes from \emph{īnferus}, \textquotedblleft{}lower\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), as if \textquotedblleft{}on the lower side\textquotedblright{}. English \emph{inferior} belongs to the same family.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[intrā]{intrā — inside, within}

\label{lesson:LA-C102-intra}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for above, then the Latin for below.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: intrā}
\textbf{intrā} — \textquotedblleft{}inside, within\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{intrā} is contracted from \emph{interā}, \textquotedblleft{}on the inner side\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{parte}, \textquotedblleft{}side\textquotedblright{}, understood (Lewis \& Short); it belongs with \emph{inter}, \textquotedblleft{}between\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[extrā]{extrā — outside, beyond}

\label{lesson:LA-C102-extra}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for below, then the Latin for inside.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: extrā}
\textbf{extrā} — \textquotedblleft{}outside, beyond\textquotedblright{}. English \emph{extra}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{extrā} is contracted from \emph{exterā}, \textquotedblleft{}on the outer side\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{exter}, \textquotedblleft{}being on the outside\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1). Old Latin wrote \emph{extrād} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}
